Heavy rain raises flash flood risk across southern Thailand

 Heavy rain raises flash flood risk across southern Thailand
 THURSDAY, NOVEMBER 19, 2026 | The Nation Editorial Team สลับเป็นเสียงผู้ชาย Play Loading... Thailand’s weather agency expects very heavy rain in parts of the South on 20 November, with flash flood risks and waves exceeding three metres in the lower Gulf.
 The Thai Meteorological Department (TMD) issued a warning on Thursday (19 November 2026) of heavy to very heavy rain across southern Thailand through 22 November, raising concerns about flash floods, overflowing waterways and landslides.
 The department urged residents, particularly those living near waterways, foothills and low-lying areas, to remain alert to the dangers of prolonged rainfall and accumulated runoff.
 For the 24-hour period ending at 6pm on 20 November, thundershowers are expected across 60% of the southern east coast, with isolated very heavy rain in Nakhon Si Thammarat, Phatthalung and Songkhla.
 Heavy rain is also expected in Surat Thani, Pattani, Yala and Narathiwat. Temperatures along the east coast are forecast to range from 21–24°C to 30–33°C.
 On the Andaman coast, thundershowers are expected across 60% of the area, with isolated heavy rain in Krabi, Trang and Satun. Temperatures will range from 23–25°C to 32–35°C.
 Strong winds and rough seas are also expected as the northeast monsoon strengthens over the Gulf of Thailand, the South and the Andaman Sea.
 From Nakhon Si Thammarat southwards, easterly winds of 20–40 kilometres per hour will generate waves of 2–3 metres, exceeding three metres in areas experiencing thundershowers.
 From Surat Thani northwards, northeasterly winds of 15–35 kilometres per hour will produce waves of 1–2 metres, rising above two metres in thundershowers.
 Along the Andaman coast, easterly winds of 15–35 kilometres per hour will bring waves of approximately one metre, increasing to 1–2 metres offshore and exceeding two metres in thundershowers.
 The department advised vessels in the Gulf of Thailand and the Andaman Sea to navigate cautiously and avoid areas affected by thundershowers. Small boats in the lower Gulf should remain ashore through 22 November.

 November 18, 2026 Meanwhile, upper Thailand is expected to experience cooler temperatures and strong winds as another moderate to rather strong high-pressure system from China extends across the region and the South China Sea.
 Over 19–22 November, temperatures in the Northeast are forecast to fall by 3–5°C, while other parts of upper Thailand will see declines of 1–3°C.
 For the latest 24-hour forecast, the Northeast will experience a temperature drop of 2–3°C, accompanied by cool mornings and strong winds. Minimum temperatures will range from 19–22°C, with highs of 33–35°C. Mountain summits will be cooler to cold, with temperatures of 13–16°C and northeasterly winds of 15–30 kilometres per hour.
 The North will experience cool and foggy mornings, with thundershowers covering 10% of the region, mainly in Mae Hong Son, Chiang Mai, Chiang Rai, Phayao and Nan.
 Temperatures in the North will range from 20–24°C to 29–35°C, while mountain peaks will experience colder conditions of 10–15°C. Easterly winds will reach 10–20 kilometres per hour.
 The Central region will see temperatures fall by 1–2°C, accompanied by strong winds. Minimum temperatures will range from 22–25°C, with highs of 33–35°C and northeasterly winds of 10–25 kilometres per hour.
 Similar conditions are expected in the East, where temperatures will drop by 1–2°C. Minimum temperatures will range from 23–25°C, with highs of 33–36°C and northeasterly winds of 15–35 kilometres per hour. Coastal waves will reach 1–2 metres, exceeding two metres offshore.
 Bangkok and surrounding provinces will also experience a temperature decline of 1–2°C, with strong northeasterly winds of 10–25 kilometres per hour. Minimum temperatures will range from 24–26°C, while daytime highs will reach 33–36°C.
 The department advised residents of upper Thailand to take precautions against changing weather conditions and urged farmers to protect their crops from potential damage.
